newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal declares war on red tape.
newsitem.headline: Portugal declares war on red tape.

text.p: The Portuguese government marked "National Anti-Bureaucracy Day" on Thursday with pledges to untangle the red tape that has wrapped itself around every aspect of public life for decades.
Ministers announced a range of reforms to simplify everything from buying a house to setting up a company.

Committed to more open government, the ruling Socialists even opened an Internet page which takes users on a tour of the official residence of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and provides details of his agenda and speeches.
But to the queues of people waiting at government offices, courts and hospitals -- it may all sound a little familiar.
"We've been having a National Anti-Bureaucracy Day for years and, apart from the odd exception, the bureaucracy remains on top with the citizen underneath," wrote Cesar Camacho in the daily Publico.
Despite efforts to reform Portugal's byzantine legal system, cases still drag through over-burdened courts for years.
Recent figures show that most Portuguese despair of receiving treatment as hospital outpatients and usually opt for a short cut through the casualty ward.

Publico reported that Lisbon's Drivers and Vehicles Office (DVL), which has won awards for its increased efficiency, was struggling to resolve the case of a driver who has been waiting to change his licence for 16 years. No DVL officials were available to comment on the report.
Journalists attempting to contact ministry spokesmen on Anti-Bureaucracy Day were asked what the subject was then told to send a fax setting out their questions.
